title: The Haunting
opening_scene: Will the investigators accept Knott's commission, and where will they begin their inquiry?
one_liner: In 1920 Boston, a landlord hires you to investigate the infamous Corbitt House—the former tenants went mad, neighbors say it is haunted, and someone who should never have been buried lies beneath the basement. Ready to play without the scenario PDF.
win_condition: The investigators uncover the truth behind the phenomena at the Corbitt House, destroy Walter Corbitt's undead body in the basement confrontation (ideally reducing him to ash with his own ritual dagger), and leave the property in a state the landlord can manage again.
summary: An original derivative introductory investigation set in 1920s Boston. A landlord hires the investigators to clear the reputation of a house whose tenants have suffered accidents, illness, and madness. Research routes (newspaper morgue, hall of records, neighbors, previous tenants) converge on the Corbitt house, where an undead sorcerer still animates his buried corpse in the sealed basement.
player_safe_summary: In autumn 1920, Boston landlord Steven Knott inherits an old house no tenant will keep. A disaster drove the former tenants, the Macarios, from the house and left members of the family in an asylum; neighbors call the place the Corbitt House. Knott hires you by the day to uncover what is wrong and clear its reputation—you can begin at the newspaper, the Hall of Records, with neighbors and former tenants, or take the key and go straight to the house.
keeper_secret_summary: Walter Corbitt's body is buried behind a partition in the house's basement. His mind survives, preserving his identity through Mythos magic and animating the corpse. He misleads and terrorizes intruders before trying to murder them. His ritual dagger can bypass his sorcery and reduce him to ash.
author: Original classic scenario structure: Sandy Petersen / Chaosium. Narrative pack adaptation: chatrpgv4 contributors (original derivative prose; does not reproduce Chaosium Product Identity text).
